# Where the HTML Guidelines get their styling

**N.B. these notes were generated by Claude Opus 5.5**

The CSS that shapes the HTML Guidelines (`P5/Guidelines-web/<lang>/html/`) is spread across CSS files, XSLT, an HTML snippet and JavaScript. This is a map of those places.

## Build

`P5/Makefile`, target `html-web.stamp`:

1. Generates `P5/Utilities/guidelines.xsl` from `P5/Utilities/guidelines.xsl.model`, using `guidelines_model_2_executable.xslt`. Edit the `.model` file, not the generated one.
2. Copies `odd.css guidelines.css guidelines-print.css teic.css` and the whole `P5/webnav/` directory into each `Guidelines-web/<lang>/html/`.
3. Runs the stylesheet through `P5/antbuildweb.xml`. The model imports `odds/odd2html.xsl` and `odds/guidelines.xsl` from the TEI Stylesheets repository.

## CSS files

| File | Linked from pages? | Role |
|---|---|---|
| `P5/guidelines.css` | yes (`cssFile`) | Main layout. Line 1 `@import`s `https://tei-c.org/css/teic.css`, which is Bootstrap 5.3 plus the site's styles. Responsive rules are at the end of the file. |
| `P5/odd.css` | yes (`cssSecondaryFile`) | Reference and spec pages (`ref-*.html`, `wovenodd` tables, A–Z index). Responsive rules are at the end of the file. |
| `P5/guidelines-print.css` | yes, `media="print"` (`cssPrintFile`) | Print styles. |
| `P5/teic.css` | no | Local Bootstrap copy. It's copied into the build but pages `@import` the live tei-c.org version instead, so it may be stale. |
| `P5/webnav/treeview.css` | no | Copied in with `webnav/` and not linked. |
| `P5/guidelines-print-beta.css` | no | Not copied into the build. |
| `P5/Source/Guidelines/guidelines-web.css` | no | Placeholder, unused. |
| `TEIC/teic.css`, `TEICSS/tei.css` | no | Unrelated to the HTML Guidelines. |

## CSS set in XSLT (`P5/Utilities/guidelines.xsl.model`)

- The `cssFile`, `cssSecondaryFile` and `cssPrintFile` params, near the top, name the stylesheets linked in each page.
- `javascriptHook` emits the `<meta name="viewport">` tag. It's in this template because this is the `<head>` hook we own: `metaHTML` lives upstream in `Stylesheets/odds/guidelines.xsl`. Without this tag, mobile browsers lay pages out at about 980px and never apply the `@media` rules.
- `startDivHook` writes inline `style` attributes on the chapter subtoc.
- `bodyEndHook` builds the footer from Bootstrap utility classes (`py-3`, `nav`, `text-body-secondary`, …).
- The upstream TEI Stylesheets also emit inline styles, such as `style="float: right;"` on bookmark links and `style="width:…"` on images taken from `graphic/@width`.

## CSS in HTML templates

- `P5/Utilities/nav.html` is the Bootstrap navbar, with an inline `style` holding the background colour. It's only included when the build runs with `GOOGLEANALYTICS=true` (the tei-c.org build, `make teiwebsiteguidelines`).

## CSS set from JavaScript

- The inline scripts in `javascriptHook` (`guidelines.xsl.model`) toggle `display` on the RELAX NG views and TOC trees. They also give the "out-of-date translation" SVG an inline `style`.
- `P5/webnav/popupFootnotes.js` sets `display` and `top` on `#footnotePopup`. Its width comes from `guidelines.css`.
- `https://tei-c.org/js/main.js` is the Bootstrap JS bundle, which handles the navbar collapse and dropdowns. It injects no stylesheet.

## Responsive breakpoint

Both `guidelines.css` and `odd.css` use `@media (max-width: 767.98px)`, which is Bootstrap's `md` breakpoint, so the layout switches at the same width as the navbar collapse.
